names.note: Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Μαΐου, «Αγίες Ακυλίνα και Καλλινίκη», with the rank word left off; the page's own head line for her is «Αγια Καλλινικη (; - 251)».

death.note: saint.gr gives the year only in the head line over her name, «Αγια Καλλινικη (; - 251)», and the body of the page gives none: it says only that the two were sent by the emperor Decius, whose reign ended in 251.

source.text: saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Μαΐου — «Αγίες Ακυλίνα και Καλλινίκη»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 9 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing, and gives her her own head line beside Aquilina's, which is why the pair is two folders. **She is not `kalloni-mother-of-gregory-palamas`**, whom the name sweep raised on the fold of the name, and not one of the corpus's male Callinici of Caesarea, Cilicia or Edessa: this is a woman, one of two sent by Decius to Christopher, whose day this also is. No place, no judge of her own, no relics, no hymn.
